title: A bill to extend the authority for commitments for the paycheck protection program and separate amounts authorized for other loans under section 7(a) of the Small Business Act, and for other purposes.
official_summary: This bill extends through August 8, 2020, the application period for the Paycheck Protection Program established to support small businesses in response to COVID-19 (i.e., coronavirus disease 2019).

summary.headline: Extends the deadline for lenders to approve Paycheck Protection Program loans for small businesses until August 8, 2020.
summary.what_it_does: This law moves the end date for the Paycheck Protection Program, a COVID-19 relief effort for small businesses, to August 8, 2020. It also separates the loan amounts set aside for the Paycheck Protection Program from amounts for other Small Business Act section 7(a) loans. The official summary covers only the deadline extension, so other provisions in the title may have details not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses seeking Paycheck Protection Program loans
who_it_affects.how: They get more time to apply for these loans before the program's application period closes.

who_it_affects.group: Lenders that make Paycheck Protection Program loans
who_it_affects.how: They can keep approving these loans under the program until the new deadline.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 4, 2020, with the extended application period running through August 8, 2020.
